messages.content: Write a note to my son's class teacher asking her to let him leave at 12 tomorrow for a dentist appointment. Around 50 words. I'm his mother, Lakshmi Rao; he is Vihaan, Class 3A.

Dear Ma'am,
My son Vihaan of Class 3A has a dental appointment tomorrow at 12:45 pm. Could you please allow him to leave school at 12 noon? I will collect him from the main gate myself. He will complete any work he misses.
Thank you,
Lakshmi Rao
Describe the smell and taste of fresh jalebis from a street stall in about 80 words, for a descriptive writing exercise.

The jalebi stall at the corner is easy to find, because the smell reaches you first. Hot ghee and warm sugar fill the air as the cook swirls orange batter into a wide pan. The spirals hiss, puff and turn golden in seconds. Then they slide into a bath of thick syrup. The first bite is crisp, then soft and sticky inside, so sweet that it almost stings. Your fingers stay sticky for an hour, and you do not mind.
My friend Nikhil is moving to Pune next week. Write a farewell card message from our group, about 60 words.

Dear Nikhil,
We can't believe you are leaving already! The canteen will feel too quiet without your terrible jokes and your loud laugh. Thank you for every late-night study session, every cricket match and every shared plate of noodles. Pune is lucky to get you. Promise to visit us in the holidays.
Missing you already,
Rohan, Ishita, Farah and Dev
Draft a short email to my team saying the Friday meeting is moved to Monday at 11 am. Under 60 words. Sign it Meenakshi.

Subject: Friday meeting moved to Monday
Hi team,
The weekly review meeting planned for this Friday has been moved to Monday at 11 am, in the same conference room. Please bring your updated task lists. If Monday doesn't work for you, let me know by Thursday.
Thanks,
Meenakshi
Write a diary entry, roughly 100 words, from a 10-year-old who saw a peacock dance for the first time.

Dear Diary,
Today was the best day of the summer holidays! We went to Mama's farm, and just after it started drizzling, a peacock came out from behind the mango trees. Suddenly he lifted his tail and opened it like a giant green and blue fan. Then he turned round and round, shaking his feathers so they made a rustling sound. I held my breath so I wouldn't scare him. Mama said peacocks dance when rain is coming. I tried to draw him tonight, but my picture doesn't look half as beautiful. I will never forget it.
Tell a tiny story of about 120 words about a grandfather teaching his granddaughter to ride a bicycle.

Every evening, Dadu held the back of Anya's blue bicycle and jogged beside her down the colony lane. "Look ahead, not at your feet," he kept saying. Anya wobbled, squealed and fell into the hedge twice. On the fifth evening, she was pedalling hard and chatting about her school play when she noticed that Dadu's voice sounded far away. She turned her head. He was standing at the gate, waving both hands in the air. Anya had ridden all the way to the corner by herself. She was so surprised that she almost fell again. Instead, she rang her bell three times, turned carefully and rode back to him, grinning. Dadu pretended he wasn't out of breath.
My colleague Suresh had a minor surgery. Write a get-well-soon message from the office, about 40 words.

Dear Suresh,
We hope you are recovering well and feeling a little stronger each day. The office isn't the same without your morning updates and your filter coffee. Take all the rest you need. We'll see you when you're ready.
Best wishes from all of us
Write a Diwali greeting for our neighbours, three sentences only.

Wishing you and your family a very happy Diwali, full of light, laughter and sweets. May the coming year bring good health and peace to your home. Thank you for being such kind and helpful neighbours all year.
I'm on a school trip to Jaipur. Write a short message to my parents, about 50 words, telling them we reached safely and what we did on day one.

Hi Ma and Papa,
We reached Jaipur safely this morning. The train was late, but nobody minded because we played antakshari the whole way. Today we visited Amber Fort and climbed so many steps! The hotel food is good. I'm tired but very happy. I'll call you tomorrow night.
Love,
Tanvi
Write a paragraph of about 90 words for teenagers on why keeping a small savings jar is useful.

A savings jar may look like a childish idea, but it teaches a grown-up lesson. When you drop in a few coins or a small note each week, you can actually see your money grow. That makes it easier to wait for something you really want instead of spending on every small temptation. It also helps you notice where your pocket money usually goes. Best of all, the day you open the jar and buy that book or pair of headphones with your own savings feels wonderful.
Write a short speech, around 100 words, for a school sports captain to give at the opening of sports day.

Good morning, respected Principal, teachers, parents and my dear friends.
Today is the day we have trained for all term. Our runners, jumpers and throwers have practised early in the mornings and late in the evenings, and today they finally get to show what they can do. But sports day is not only about medals. It is about trying your best, cheering for others and shaking hands at the finish line, whether you win or lose. So run hard, play fair and enjoy every moment. Let's make this a day to remember.
Thank you.
Write a 60-word description of my dog, a lazy old Labrador called Bruno, for my class blog.

Bruno is our eleven-year-old Labrador, and he is the laziest member of the family. He spends most of the day stretched across the cool floor near the front door, so everyone has to step over him. His golden fur has turned white around his nose. He only runs when he hears the fridge door open. We love him completely.
I want to tell my mother I'm sorry for shouting at her this morning. Help me write a message, about 50 words. I'm 16.

Ma, I'm sorry I shouted at you this morning. I was stressed about my test, but that's no reason to speak to you like that. You were only trying to help. I'll make tea for both of us when I get home, and I'd like to talk properly. Love you.
Draft a notice of about 60 words informing residents that the water supply will be off on Wednesday from 10 am to 4 pm because of tank cleaning.

NOTICE: Water Supply Interruption
Water supply to all flats will be stopped on Wednesday from 10 am to 4 pm while the overhead tanks are cleaned. Please store enough water for cooking, drinking and washing before 10 am. We are sorry for the inconvenience and thank you for your cooperation.
- Building Maintenance Team
Write a short book review for my school library board, about 80 words, of Alice's Adventures in Wonderland.

Alice's Adventures in Wonderland by Lewis Carroll begins when a bored girl follows a White Rabbit down a rabbit hole. What follows is a dream full of strange creatures: a grinning Cheshire Cat, a mad tea party and a bad-tempered Queen who keeps shouting "Off with her head!" Alice keeps growing and shrinking, and nothing makes sense for long. The book is short, funny and full of clever word games. I recommend it to anyone who enjoys nonsense and surprises.
Rating: 4 out of 5
Write an application to the principal asking for permission to start a gardening club, around 100 words. I'm Ritika, Class 9C.

To
The Principal
Subject: Permission to start a gardening club
Respected Ma'am,
I am Ritika from Class 9C. Some of my classmates and I would like to start a gardening club in our school. We would like to use the empty patch of land behind the science block to grow vegetables and flowers. We plan to meet twice a week during the activity period, with Mr. Thomas, our biology teacher, as our guide. The club would teach us patience, teamwork and care for nature. We would be grateful for your permission.
Yours obediently,
Ritika
Class 9C
Write a funny invite for a movie night at my flat this Friday, around 40 words. Everyone should bring their own snacks.

Movie night at my flat this Friday at 8 pm! I have the films, the cushions and a very small sofa. You bring the snacks, because my kitchen currently contains half a lemon and some salt. Pyjamas are welcome.
Write a short professional bio, about 60 words, in third person, for Neha Joshi, a 24-year-old primary school teacher who loves storytelling.

Neha Joshi is a primary school teacher with two years of experience teaching Classes 2 and 3. She believes children learn best when lessons feel like stories, so she often uses puppets, songs and picture books in her classroom. Neha is currently training to run reading clubs for young learners. Outside school, she writes short stories and enjoys long train journeys.
Describe a winter morning in a hill town in 5 sentences.

Thick fog hung over the hill town, hiding the pine trees until you were almost beside them. Smoke curled from the chimneys of the small wooden houses along the slope. A shopkeeper rubbed his hands together while he rolled up his shutter. Children in woollen caps walked to school, their breath making little clouds in the cold air. By nine o'clock, the sun broke through, and the snowy peaks appeared like a surprise.
Can I get a tiny story about a boy who tries to cook dinner for his parents and burns the rice? 100 words.

Ishaan wanted to surprise his parents on their anniversary, so he decided to cook dinner by himself. He chopped onions with watering eyes, made a careful dal and put the rice on the stove. Then he went to decorate the table with paper flowers. Ten minutes later, a burning smell filled the flat. The rice was black at the bottom. Ishaan almost cried. When his parents came home, they found him scraping the pot. His father laughed and tasted the dal. "Perfect," he said. "And the rice has a smoky flavour." They ate the top layer together, smiling.
Write a short birthday wish for my little sister turning 5. Two sentences, very sweet.
Happy fifth birthday to the brightest little star in our home! I hope your day is full of cake, balloons and giggles, and that you always keep that big, beautiful smile.
Write a paragraph, about 80 words, about keeping a tidy study desk.

A tidy study desk makes studying feel less like a battle. When books, pens and notes each have a place, you do not waste ten minutes searching for a ruler before you start. A clear desk also helps the mind feel calmer, because there is less to distract you. It only takes five minutes at the end of each day to put things away. Try it for a week, and you may be surprised by how much easier it is to sit down and begin.
My cousin from London is visiting Kolkata for the first time. Write a welcome message to her, about 70 words. Her name is Emily.

Dear Emily,
Welcome to Kolkata! We are so happy you are finally here. Get ready for crowded trams, yellow taxis and the best sweets you will ever taste. This weekend, we will take you to the Victoria Memorial and for a boat ride on the Hooghly. Ma has already planned a lunch of fish curry and mishti doi. Please tell us if you feel tired or need anything at all.
Love,
Sohini
Write a diary entry of around 90 words by a 14-year-old who felt left out at lunch today.

Dear Diary,
Lunch was hard today. Mira and Sana sat at a different table and kept laughing about something I didn't understand. I sat with my book and pretended to read, but I couldn't concentrate. Maybe they didn't mean to leave me out, but it still hurt. On the way home, I talked to Ma, and she said friendships have bumpy days too. Tomorrow I will just ask them if they want to sit together. If they don't, I'll try sitting with the new girl, Joanne.
Write a thank-you message, under 50 words, to my classmate who shared his notes when I was absent for a week. His name is Faizan.

Thank you so much, Faizan! Your notes saved me this week. They were neat, complete and much easier to follow than my own. I would have been completely lost in the maths test without them. I owe you a samosa, or maybe two.
Describe a crowded local train in the morning rush hour, around 90 words.

At 8:15 am, the local train pulls in already full. Before it even stops, people leap onto the steps, gripping the poles with one hand and their bags with the other. Inside, there is no space to move. Someone's elbow is in your ribs, and someone else's tiffin bag presses against your back. A college student reads notes over a stranger's shoulder. An old man sings softly near the door. Fans whirl overhead without doing much. Yet at each station, more people somehow squeeze in, and nobody seems surprised.
I'm a freelance illustrator called Aisha. Write a polite message to a client asking for payment of an overdue invoice, about 70 words.

Dear Mr. Kapoor,
I hope you are doing well. This is a gentle reminder that the invoice for the book cover illustrations, sent on 3rd March, is now two weeks overdue. I have attached a copy for your reference. I would be grateful if you could arrange the payment this week. Please tell me if there is any problem with the invoice.
Thank you,
Aisha
Write a paragraph of 80 words about how my family celebrates Eid.

Eid in our home begins before sunrise. Abba goes to the mosque for the morning prayer, while Ammi finishes the sheer khurma she started the night before. We all wear new clothes, and the younger children wait eagerly for their eidi from the elders. Through the day, relatives and neighbours visit, and the table never stays empty for long. In the evening, we take plates of sweets to friends. For us, Eid is about gratitude, forgiveness and an open door.
Write a short story for kids, about 100 words, about a goldfish that wants to see the world.

Goldie the goldfish lived in a round bowl on the kitchen windowsill. Every day she watched birds fly past and wondered what lay beyond the garden wall. One morning, a little girl named Pooja pressed her nose to the glass. "Do you want to see more?" she asked. Goldie flicked her tail. That afternoon, Pooja carried the bowl carefully around the house. Goldie saw the living room, the bookshelf, the colourful curtains and even the sleeping cat, who opened one eye. When she was back on the windowsill, Goldie decided that her bowl had the best view after all.
Congratulate my daughter's football team on reaching the finals. A message for their group, about 40 words, from the assistant coach.

Well done, girls! Reaching the finals is a fantastic achievement. You passed well, defended bravely and never gave up, even when we were a goal down. Rest well this week, practise hard on Thursday, and let's play the final with the same spirit.
I lent my friend 500 rupees two months ago. Write a polite reminder message, about 40 words, that won't hurt our friendship.

Hey Kunal, hope you're doing well! Just a small reminder about the 500 rupees I lent you in August. No rush if things are tight, but could you send it back sometime this month? Thanks, and let's catch up soon.
Write a 4-line description of the sea at sunset for my travel scrapbook. Each line should be one sentence.

The sun sank slowly into the sea like a ripe orange.
The waves turned pink and gold as they rolled onto the sand.
Fishing boats came home with their nets folded on deck.
A cool wind carried the smell of salt and roasted corn.
Write a letter of about 120 words to my grandfather in the village, telling him about my new school.

Dear Dadaji,
I hope you are well and that your knees are not troubling you much this winter. I have some news. I started at my new school last Monday. It is much bigger than my old one, with three floors and a huge playground. On the first day I felt nervous, but a boy called Samuel showed me around, and now we sit together. My favourite subject is science, because our teacher lets us do experiments every Friday. The canteen samosas are good, but not as good as Dadi's. I miss our evening walks to the fields. Please write back and tell me about the new calf.
Your loving grandson,
Abhay
My son is starting kindergarten. Write a short note, about 50 words, to put in his lunch box on day one.

Good morning, my brave boy! Today is your very first day of school. Eat your lunch, play nicely and listen to your teacher. If you feel shy, look at this note and remember that Mumma loves you very much. I will be waiting for you at the gate at 12 o'clock.
Write a 70-word paragraph for a school assembly about why libraries still matter.

In a world full of screens, a library is still a special place. It is quiet, it is free, and it is open to everyone, whether you are rich or poor, young or old. On its shelves you can travel to old Russia, a whaling ship or a castle in the hills. A library also teaches patience, because a good book cannot be rushed. Let's use ours more often.
Write a message for our society's group, around 60 words, asking for volunteers to help organise the children's drawing competition on 15 August.

Hello everyone,
We are holding a drawing competition for children on 15 August at 10 am in the clubhouse. We need about six volunteers to help with registration, handing out paper and colours, and keeping the little ones happy. It will take only two hours. If you can help, please reply to this message by Sunday.
Thank you!
Sunita, Cultural Committee
What does homesickness feel like for a first-year college student? Put it into a paragraph of about 80 words.

Homesickness arrives quietly. It stays away during lectures and busy afternoons, but it creeps in at night, when the hostel corridor goes silent. You miss small things most: the whistle of the pressure cooker, your father reading the newspaper aloud, the way your mother calls you for dinner three times. The mess food tastes of nothing. You look through old photos and feel a lump in your throat. Then a friend knocks with two cups of tea, and this place starts to feel a little like home.
Write a tiny story, around 110 words, about a girl who misses her train but has an adventure anyway.

Rhea reached the platform just in time to see the last carriage of her express train disappear around the bend. Her heart sank. The next train was in four hours. Grumbling, she bought a cup of tea and sat on a bench beside an old woman with a basket of guavas. The woman turned out to be a retired headmistress who had travelled all over the country by train. She told Rhea about sleeping on a station floor in Assam and being chased by a goat in Rajasthan. Rhea laughed so much that she almost forgot the time. When her train finally came, she was sorry to say goodbye.
Write a resignation note, about 90 words, polite and positive, from Joseph, who is leaving a bakery job to study further.

Dear Mrs. D'Souza,
Please accept this letter as notice of my resignation from my position at Sweet Crumbs Bakery. My last working day will be 30th June. I have been accepted into a two-year course in food technology, and I want to give it my full attention. I am very grateful for everything I have learned here, from kneading dough at dawn to handling busy festival orders. Thank you for your patience and kindness. I will gladly help train my replacement before I leave.
Warm regards,
Joseph
Write a short, encouraging note for my friend who has just started running every morning. About 40 words.

Look at you, waking up before the sun! Starting a running habit is the hardest part, and you've already done it. Go at your own pace, enjoy the quiet streets and don't worry about speed yet. I'm proud of you.
Write a 60-word message to my flatmates asking everyone to wash their own dishes on time. Friendly, not bossy.

Hi all,
Quick request: could we each try to wash our own dishes on the same day we use them? The sink has been full most mornings, and it's making breakfast a bit difficult. I know everyone is busy, so even a quick rinse helps. Thanks, and I'll keep doing my share too!
Ankita
Write a description of an old bookshop in a busy city lane, about 100 words.

Squeezed between a mobile repair shop and a sweet stall, the old bookshop is easy to miss. Its doorway is narrow, and inside, the shelves reach right up to the ceiling. Books are stacked on the floor too, in leaning towers that look ready to fall. The air smells of dust and old paper. A ceiling fan turns slowly above the counter, where the owner, a thin man with round glasses, sits reading. He barely looks up when you enter. But if you ask for a book, he will find it in seconds, pulling it from a pile without even searching.
Write a message to a friend I haven't spoken to in two years, about 60 words. I want to reconnect without it feeling awkward.

Hi Leela,
It's been far too long! I was going through old photos today and found one from our school trip to Ooty, with both of us wrapped in blankets. It made me smile and miss you. How have you been? I'd love to catch up properly, maybe over a phone call this weekend if you're free.
Shreya
Write a short speech of about 80 words for a student thanking teachers on Teachers' Day.

Good morning to all our teachers.
Today we want to say something we do not say often enough: thank you. Thank you for explaining the same sum five times without losing patience. Thank you for noticing when we were quiet and for believing in us even when we did not believe in ourselves. You teach us much more than subjects. You teach us how to be good people. Happy Teachers' Day, and please enjoy the cake. We baked it ourselves.
Write a note, around 50 words, to my husband reminding him about our daughter's parent-teacher meeting tomorrow at 9 am.

Hi Sameer,
Just a reminder that Anika's parent-teacher meeting is tomorrow at 9 am in Room 12. I have a client call then, so please go and take her report card with you. Ask Ms. Bose about her maths homework too. Call me afterwards and tell me how it went.
Ruchi
Write a tiny story of about 90 words about an old tree that is going to be cut down, and the children who save it.

The old neem tree at the end of Station Road had given shade for sixty years. One Monday, a notice appeared on its trunk: it would be cut down to widen the road. The children of the lane were shocked. That evening, they made posters, collected signatures from every house and met the ward officer with their parents. They explained how birds nested in it and how vendors rested beneath it. A week later, a new notice appeared. The road would curve gently around the tree instead. The children held a picnic under it to celebrate.
Write an 80-word paragraph for a self-improvement club newsletter on making a to-do list each evening.

Making a to-do list each evening is a small habit with a big effect. Before bed, take five minutes to write down the three most important tasks for tomorrow. This clears your head, so you are less likely to lie awake remembering things you forgot. In the morning, you can start working straight away instead of wondering where to begin. Keep the list short and realistic. Crossing off each task through the day gives a quiet sense of progress that keeps you going.
Write a short review, about 60 words, of a homestay we stayed at in Coorg, for their guest book.

Thank you, Ponnappa family, for a wonderful three days! Waking up to mist over the coffee plantation was magical, and the food was the best part of our trip. We will dream about your bamboo shoot curry and homemade jam. The children loved feeding the ducks. We felt like guests in a family home, not a hotel.
With thanks, the Menons
Write a short message, around 50 words, to a friend whose grandmother passed away. Keep it gentle.

Dear Nandini,
I'm so sorry to hear about your grandmother. I know how close you were and how much she meant to you. I don't have the right words, but I'm here for you, whether you want to talk or just sit quietly together. Sending you a big hug.
Fatima
Write a description, about 70 words, of the last over of a tense gully cricket match.

Six runs needed off the last over, and the whole lane had gone silent. Aman wiped his forehead and gripped the taped tennis ball. Kids crowded the balconies, and even the vegetable seller had stopped to watch. The first ball was a dot. The second went for two. Then Bittu swung hard, and the ball flew over the neighbour's wall. Everyone screamed, half in joy and half in fear. Aunty would definitely not give it back.
Could you draft an email to my professor asking for a two-day extension on my lab report? I'm Kiran Patil, a second-year B.Sc. student. About 80 words.

Subject: Request for a short extension on the lab report
Dear Professor Menon,
I am writing to ask for a two-day extension on the physics lab report due this Friday. My grandmother was unwell last week, and I spent several days helping my family at home. I have finished the experiment and most of the analysis, but I need a little more time to complete the discussion section. Could I submit it on Sunday evening instead?
Thank you for considering my request.
Kiran Patil, B.Sc. Second Year
Please write a paragraph, about 90 words, about why I love collecting stamps. I'm 12.

I started collecting stamps when my uncle gave me an old album he had kept since college. At first I just liked the bright colours, but soon I began to notice the stories behind them. One stamp shows a tiger from the Sundarbans, and another shows a sailing ship from a country I had never heard of. Each one makes me curious, so I look it up in the atlas. Now I have more than three hundred stamps. My dream is to find one from every country in the world.
Our new neighbours just moved in next door. Write a welcome note to leave with a box of sweets, about 50 words.

Dear new neighbours,
Welcome to Lotus Apartments! We are the Sharmas from Flat 204, right next door. We hope you are settling in well. Please enjoy these sweets, and don't hesitate to knock if you need anything, whether it is a screwdriver or directions to the market.
Warm wishes,
Pallavi and Arun
Need a description of a summer afternoon in a small town during a power cut, around 100 words.

At two in the afternoon, the power goes off, and the whole town seems to sigh. Ceiling fans slow down and stop. The heat presses against the windows like a heavy blanket. In the lanes, nothing moves except a stray dog looking for shade under a parked scooter. Grandmothers fan themselves with folded newspapers on the verandas. Children are told to lie down and rest, but they whisper and giggle instead. A street vendor calls out lazily, selling kulfi from a box wrapped in red cloth. Everyone waits for the cheerful whirr that means the power is back.
Help me write a short message inviting my cousins to my first sitar recital next Sunday at 6 pm. About 50 words.

Hi everyone! After two years of practice, I'm finally giving my first sitar recital next Sunday at 6 pm at Kala Bhavan hall. I'll be playing two short pieces, so it won't be long, I promise. It would mean a lot to see your faces in the audience. Please come!
Put together a short out-of-office reply for my work email, under 50 words. I'm away from 10 to 17 May; my colleague Divya Rao handles urgent matters.

Thank you for your email. I am on leave from 10 May to 17 May and will have limited access to email. For urgent matters, please contact my colleague Divya Rao. I will reply to your message as soon as I return.
Compose a recipe card intro, about 60 words, for my mother's famous lemon rice, for a family cookbook.

Every family has one dish that means home, and for us it is Amma's lemon rice. She made it for every train journey, every school picnic and every lazy Sunday lunch. It is tangy, bright yellow and crunchy with peanuts and curry leaves. It takes only twenty minutes, yet somehow nobody else's version ever tastes quite the same.
I need a sorry note for my friend Zara. I cancelled our plans at the last minute twice this month. Under 60 words.

Zara, I'm really sorry for cancelling on you twice this month, especially at the last minute. That wasn't fair to you, and I know you had made time for me. You deserve better than that. Let me make it up to you: you pick the day and the place, and I promise I'll be there.
For a nature magazine for kids, write about 100 words on what happens in a pond during the monsoon.

When the monsoon arrives, a quiet pond suddenly comes alive. Rainwater fills it to the brim, and the edges turn green with fresh grass. At night, frogs gather and croak loudly, calling to one another. Soon there are jelly-like clusters of eggs floating near the reeds, and in a few weeks, tiny tadpoles wriggle everywhere. Dragonflies dart over the water, and water lilies open their pink flowers. Herons stand still on one leg, waiting patiently for a fish. If you sit by a pond in the monsoon, you will see a whole small world at work.
Could you write a thank-you card from my parents to my uncle, who helped us move house? Around 60 words.

Dear Ravi,
Thank you so much for all your help with our move. We could not have done it without you. You packed boxes, carried heavy furniture and even fixed the fan in the new kitchen. Most of all, your jokes kept everyone smiling on a very tiring day. Please come for dinner soon.
With love and thanks,
Mohan and Geeta
Our office is celebrating Christmas. Please write a short welcome note, about 50 words, to put beside the decorated tree.

Merry Christmas, everyone! This tree was decorated by all of us, one paper star at a time. Take a moment today to stop by, enjoy a slice of plum cake and add a wish for the new year on one of the cards below. Thank you for a wonderful year together.
Write a gentle bedtime story for a three-year-old, about 80 words, about a little moon who is sleepy.

High in the sky lived a little moon called Chandu. All night he shone for the owls, the cats and the night trains. When morning came, he felt very sleepy. He yawned a big silver yawn. "Goodnight, stars," he whispered. "Goodnight, clouds." The clouds tucked him in with a soft, white blanket. The sun smiled and said, "I will look after the sky now." So the little moon closed his eyes and slept until evening came again.
Please draft a polite message to my landlord asking if I can pay rent on the 7th instead of the 1st from next month. About 70 words. My name is Shalini.

Dear Mr. Bhatia,
I hope you are well. From next month, my salary will be credited on the 5th instead of the 1st because of a change at my office. Would it be possible for me to pay the rent on the 7th of each month from now on? I have always paid on time, and I will continue to do so on the new date.
Thank you for understanding,
Shalini, Flat 3B
My daughter's school wants a 50-word note from parents about what she enjoys outside school. Saanvi is 8 and loves drawing, cycling and her pet rabbit.

Outside school, Saanvi loves to draw. She fills notebook after notebook with pictures of animals, especially her pet rabbit, Coco, whom she feeds every morning. She also enjoys cycling around our colony with her friends in the evenings. She is curious and cheerful, and she asks about a hundred questions a day.
I need an email to a hotel in Shimla asking if they have a family room for 3 nights from 20 December. About 70 words. Name: Anil Varghese.

Subject: Room availability from 20 December
Dear Sir or Madam,
I would like to know if you have a family room available for three nights, from 20 December to 23 December. We are two adults and two children, aged six and nine. Could you please tell me the rate per night and whether breakfast is included? We would also prefer a room with a view of the hills, if possible.
Thank you,
Anil Varghese
Describe a kabaddi raid in about 80 words, for a sports report in our school newsletter.

With the score tied at 24 all, our captain, Harpreet, stepped across the line, chanting "kabaddi, kabaddi" without a pause. The defenders spread out in a careful half circle. She feinted left, then lunged right and touched two players before they could react. Three of them dived at her ankles, but she twisted free and stretched her hand across the midline just in time. The referee's whistle blew. Two points! The crowd roared, and our team never looked back.
Write me a short diary entry, 70 words, for a teenager who just got good news about their exam results.

Dear Diary,
I can't stop smiling! The results came out today, and I scored 91 percent. I was so nervous that I asked Didi to check the website for me. When she screamed, I thought something was wrong. Papa hugged me in front of the whole building, and Ma made kheer even though it was a weekday. All those late nights finally paid off.
Our community hall is hosting a book exchange on Saturday. Make a notice for it, about 70 words.

NOTICE: Book Exchange Day
Got books you have already read? Bring them to the Community Hall this Saturday from 10 am to 1 pm and swap them for new ones. Story books, novels, comics and cookbooks are all welcome. Please make sure the books are clean and complete. Children's books will be kept on a separate table. Any books left over will be donated to the local school library.
- Residents' Welfare Association
Can you write a short message thanking my team for working late to finish the launch? About 50 words. I'm the manager.

Hi team,
Thank you for all the late evenings this week. Because of your hard work, we finished the launch on time, and the client is very happy. I know it wasn't easy, especially with the last-minute changes. Please take Friday afternoon off. You have earned it.
Gauri
Tell me a 100-word story about a stray puppy that follows a boy home from school.

Every day after school, Tenzin noticed a small brown puppy sitting by the bus stop. One rainy afternoon, the puppy stood up and trotted behind him. Tenzin walked faster. The puppy walked faster too. When he reached his gate, the puppy sat down and looked up at him with big, wet eyes. Tenzin's mother came out with an umbrella. She looked at the puppy, then at her son. "Only until the rain stops," she said. The rain stopped the next morning. But by then the puppy had a name, a blanket and a bowl of his own.
For our class blog, write about 90 words on a book character I admire: Jane Eyre.

I admire Jane Eyre because she never lets other people decide her worth. As an orphan, she is treated cruelly by her aunt, Mrs. Reed, and then suffers hunger and cold at Lowood School. Yet she grows into a thoughtful, honest young woman who works as a governess. When she learns that Mr. Rochester is already married, she leaves Thornfield, even though she loves him. Later, she refuses a marriage without love. Jane shows that quiet people can be the strongest of all.
How would you describe a city street right after heavy rain? Give me about 80 words.

After the heavy rain, the city street looks freshly washed. Puddles shine in every pothole, reflecting the grey sky and the blinking traffic signals. Autos splash through the water, and people on the pavement jump back just in time. Shopkeepers sweep water out of their doorways with long brooms. The smell of wet dust mixes with the smell of frying bhajias from a corner stall. On a balcony above, a child holds out a hand to catch the last few drops.
I just finished my first pottery class. Write a short post for my personal blog about it, about 90 words.

Today I sat at a pottery wheel for the first time, and it was much harder than it looks. The clay kept wobbling and collapsing, and within minutes my hands and face were covered in mud. Our teacher, Mrs. Kulkarni, kept saying, "Slow down. Let the wheel do the work." By the end of the class, I had made one small, crooked bowl. It leans to one side and has a thumbprint on the rim, but I have never been prouder of anything. Next week, I'm trying a cup.
Write a short message, under 40 words, to my mom on Mother's Day. I'm away at college.
Happy Mother's Day, Ma! I wish I could be home today to hug you. Thank you for every call, every packed snack and every word of advice. I love you and miss you. See you very soon.
Write a notice, about 60 words, for the school notice board announcing an inter-house quiz competition.

NOTICE: Inter-House Quiz Competition
An inter-house quiz will be held on Friday, 12 July, at 11 am in the school auditorium. Each house must send a team of three students from Classes 8 to 10. Topics include science, history, sports and general knowledge. Names must be given to the house captains by Tuesday. Come and cheer for your house!
- Quiz Club
My friend is starting her own small tailoring business. Write a message wishing her success, around 50 words.

Congratulations, Rukhsar! Opening your own tailoring shop is a big, brave step, and I'm so proud of you. Your stitching has always been the neatest I've ever seen. I hope your shop is busy from the very first day. I'm coming in next week to place my first order!
Describe the view from a train window on a long journey through the countryside, roughly 100 words.

For hours, the train rolls through the countryside, and the view changes like pages in a picture book. Green paddy fields stretch to the horizon, with white egrets standing in the water. A boy on a buffalo waves as we pass. Small stations flash by, each with a tea stall, a sleepy dog and a painted name board. Then come rivers, wide and brown, crossed on long iron bridges that rattle under the wheels. Villages appear with mud walls and blue doors. As the sun sets, the sky turns orange, and the fields grow dark and quiet.
Write a short letter, around 100 words, to my future self at 25. I'm 15 now.

Dear Me at 25,
Right now, I'm fifteen, and I'm worried about maths tests, pimples and whether people like me. I hope those worries seem small to you now. I hope you still sing loudly in the shower and still love mango season. Did you become a vet, or did you change your mind? Either way is fine, as long as you are happy. Please call Nani often, and be kind to the people who were kind to me. And if you ever forget how hard you worked to get here, read this letter again.
Love,
Me at 15
Write a polite complaint to an online store about receiving a shirt in the wrong size. Under 80 words. Order number 45812.

Subject: Wrong size received, Order No. 45812
Dear Customer Support,
I recently received my order, number 45812, but the shirt is size L instead of the size M that I ordered. The shirt is unused, with all tags still attached. Could you please arrange an exchange for the correct size? I would also like to know how to return the wrong one.
Thank you for your help.
Regards,
Aditya Shetty
In about 60 words, describe a butterfly garden for a children's activity sheet.

Welcome to the butterfly garden! Here, colourful flowers grow in every corner, from orange marigolds to purple lantana. Look closely and you will see butterflies of all sizes, some yellow, some blue and some with spots like eyes. They sip nectar from the flowers. Can you count how many different colours you see? Walk softly so you don't scare them.
Can you write a goodbye note for my best friend who's going to study abroad? About 80 words. Her name is Mei.

Dear Mei,
I can't believe this is our last week together before you fly off to start your new adventure. I'll miss our long walks after class, our silly voice notes and the way you always know when something is wrong. I'm so proud of you for chasing your dream. Please eat properly, call when you're lonely and send me pictures of everything. The time difference won't stop me from bothering you.
Love you always,
Divya
Write a 70-word description of my grandmother's kitchen on a festival morning.

On festival mornings, Nani's kitchen is the busiest room in the house. Brass pots bubble on both stoves, and the smell of cardamom and ghee drifts into every corner. Bowls of soaked dal and grated coconut cover the counter. Nani moves quickly between them, giving orders to everyone who wanders in. Someone grinds chutney, someone fries puris, and someone always gets caught tasting the halwa too early.
My nephew is giving a one-minute speech on 'My Favourite Season'. Write it for him, around 120 words, in simple English. He's 9.

Good morning, everyone. My favourite season is winter. In winter, the mornings are cool and misty. I wear my warm red sweater and the woolly cap my grandmother knitted for me. I love drinking hot chocolate in the evening and eating oranges in the sun on our terrace. Winter is also the season of carrots and peas, so my mother makes gajar halwa and matar paratha. On Sundays, my family goes for picnics in the park because it is not too hot. The best part is sitting under a blanket and listening to stories at night. Winter makes me feel cosy and happy. That is why I love it the most. Thank you.
Please write a short appreciation note, about 60 words, from me to our office cleaner, Mr. Ramesh, who is moving back to his village.

Dear Ramesh ji,
Thank you for keeping our office clean and cheerful for so many years. You were always the first to arrive and the last to leave, and you greeted everyone with a smile. We will miss your stories about your village, but we are happy you are going home at last. We wish you peaceful days with your family.
With respect,
Kiran and the Accounts Team
Write about 90 words on Holi for a class magazine, from the point of view of a child.

Holi is my favourite festival because it is the only day when getting messy is allowed! On the night before, we gather around a big bonfire in our colony. The next morning, I fill my pichkari with coloured water and rush outside. Soon everyone is pink, green and yellow, even my grandfather. We chase each other, dance to loud music and eat gujiyas until our tummies hurt. In the afternoon, scrubbing off the colour takes forever. But I don't mind, because I'm already waiting for next year.
Give me a short paragraph, around 70 words, to encourage my classmates to switch off fans and lights when leaving the classroom.

Every day, our classroom fans and lights keep running long after we leave for lunch or the playground. This wastes electricity and money that our school could spend on books or sports equipment. The solution is simple. The last person to leave should check the switches before walking out. It takes just five seconds. If each class does this, our whole school can make a real difference together.
Write a short travel diary entry, about 90 words, about seeing snow for the first time near Manali.

Dear Diary,
Today I touched snow for the first time in my life! We drove up from Manali early in the morning, and suddenly the whole hillside was white. It was much colder and softer than I expected. My brother threw a snowball that hit me right on the nose. Of course, I threw three back. My gloves got soaked, and my fingers went numb, but I didn't want to leave. In the evening, we drank hot soup by the heater, and my cheeks were still tingling.
Our neighbour's dog, Simba, died yesterday. Write a short condolence note to the family, about 50 words.

Dear Joshi family,
We were so sad to hear about Simba. He was the friendliest dog in the building and always greeted us with a wagging tail. The children will miss playing with him. Please know that we are thinking of you, and do tell us if we can help in any way.
The Pintos
Write a short paragraph, under 80 words, explaining to a 7-year-old why we can't buy every toy we see.

Money is a bit like the water in your bottle. There is only so much of it, so we have to choose carefully how to use it. Mummy and Papa need money for food, school, the house and many other things. If we buy every toy we see, there won't be enough left for important things. But if we wait and choose one special toy, we can enjoy it even more.
Write a cheerful notice, about 50 words, inviting students to join the badminton club.

Love badminton? Join the School Badminton Club! We practise every Tuesday and Thursday from 4 to 5:30 pm in the indoor hall. Beginners are welcome, and rackets are available for those who don't have one. Learn new shots, make friends and get ready for the inter-school tournament. Sign up with Ms. Pereira by Friday!
I'd like a short story, about 100 words, about a family stuck at home during a thunderstorm when the lights go out.

The thunder cracked so loudly that the windows rattled, and then the lights went out. Little Arya screamed and grabbed her father's arm. "Nobody panic," said Papa, who was clearly panicking as he searched for the torch. Ma found a candle instead. The family gathered in the living room, and Dadi began telling the story of the night a storm blew the roof off her father's cowshed. Soon everyone was laughing at her funny voices. Rain drummed on the roof, but nobody noticed anymore. When the lights came back, Arya groaned. "Can we switch them off again?"
Write a friendly message, about 50 words, asking my upstairs neighbour to keep his music lower after 10 pm on weekdays.

Hi Vikram, hope you're doing well! I wanted to ask a small favour. On weekdays, the music from your flat can be heard quite clearly after 10 pm, and my son has early school. Would you mind keeping it a little lower at night? Thanks so much for understanding.
Put together an invitation, under 60 words, for a weekend sketching walk in the old part of town.

Calling all sketchers! Join us for a sketching walk through the old town this Saturday at 7 am. We will meet at the clock tower and wander through the narrow lanes, stopping to draw old doors, balconies and temple corners. Bring a sketchbook, a pencil and a water bottle. All levels are welcome. Tea afterwards!
Help me describe my first day at a new college in a diary entry of about 100 words.

Dear Diary,
Today was my first day of college, and I got lost three times before lunch. The campus is huge, with red brick buildings and a long avenue of gulmohar trees. In my first lecture, I sat in the wrong classroom for ten minutes before I realised it was a chemistry class. Everyone seemed to know where they were going except me. Then, at the canteen, a girl named Harini asked if she could share my table. We talked for an hour. By evening, the campus felt a little smaller. Tomorrow, I'll bring a map.
For our anniversary, write a short message to my wife, Priyanka. About 60 words, warm but not too flowery.

Happy anniversary, Priyanka. Seven years ago, I married my best friend, and somehow you have become even more than that. Thank you for your patience on my grumpy mornings, your laughter on long drives and the way you make our home feel warm. I'm grateful for every year with you, and I'm looking forward to many more.
Love,
Mihir
Draft a message to a job recruiter thanking her for yesterday's interview. About 70 words. I'm Rohit Malhotra, and I interviewed for a data analyst role.

Dear Ms. Sen,
Thank you for taking the time to interview me yesterday for the Data Analyst position. I enjoyed learning more about your team and the projects you are working on. Our conversation about the customer survey data made me even more excited about the role. I would be happy to share any further information you may need.
Best regards,
Rohit Malhotra
In about 80 words, describe a city park early on a Sunday morning.

Early on Sunday morning, the city park belongs to the walkers. Groups of uncles in white sneakers march around the track, arguing about cricket. A row of women does yoga on the grass near the fountain. A man sells fresh coconut water from a cart by the gate. Squirrels race up the banyan trees, and pigeons gather wherever someone scatters grain. The noise of traffic is still far away, and for an hour, the city feels gentle and slow.
My younger brother is nervous about his first day of high school. Write him an encouraging note, around 60 words.

Hey Neel,
I know you're nervous about tomorrow, and that's completely normal. Everyone feels lost on the first day, even the teachers sometimes! Just be yourself, say hello to the person next to you and ask questions when you're unsure. In a week, it will feel like you've been there forever. I'm proud of you, little brother.
Didi
Write a short invitation, about 50 words, for a potluck lunch at the office on Friday. Everyone brings one dish.

Potluck lunch this Friday! Let's take a break and eat together at 1 pm in the meeting room. Everyone is invited to bring one dish, homemade or from your favourite shop. Please add your dish to the list on the pantry door so we don't end up with five plates of biryani. See you there!
Make up an 80-word story about an elephant who is afraid of mice.

Gajju was the biggest elephant in the forest, yet he was afraid of one tiny thing: mice. Whenever he saw one, he trumpeted and ran behind a tree. The other animals laughed. One day, Gajju got his foot stuck in a hunter's net. He pulled and pulled, but it held tight. Then a small mouse appeared and began to nibble the ropes. Soon Gajju was free. "Thank you," he said softly. From that day, he was never afraid of mice again.
